acceptance.1. window 3: three candidate CI runs sta: tests/code_review_speculative_queue.rs window_of_three_starts_every_candidate_ci_before_the_first_submit_and_lands_in_order. After one tick, three distinct runs are bound to candidates c0 = merge(T, s0), c1 = merge(c0, s1) and c2 = merge(c1, s2); the target is unchanged and nothing is submitted. known_tradeoffs: The engine dispatches at most one active run per project. In a single-project review the window admits all candidate runs together, and they execute one after another; real parallelism comes from existing capacity such as monorepo affected projects.

A CI run already dispatched for a superseded candidate is ignored, not cancelled at the provider, because provider cancellation is an ambiguous external effect. It holds its project slot until it terminates. Undispatched runs are cancelled.
A failure is conclusive only at the head, so a failing non-head entry stops the window behind it until its predecessors land. This avoids ejecting an entry for an ancestor's fault.
The window starts at its ceiling, shrinks by `decrease` on each ejection, and grows by `increase` on each landing.
